items.title: Everton hold off Ipswich thanks to Thierno Barry goal despite VAR controversy

There will also be relief, for Pro Ref as well as David Moyes, that another controversial call from a video assistant referee did not impede their progress against Ipswich.Thierno Barry decided a close-fought contest with his fifth goal of the campaign. He should have had a sixth but an offside Brennan Johnson was adjudged to have impacted Ipswich goalkeeper Christian Walton’s ability to save a ball he made no attempt to save and was nowhere near saving. Unlike last weekend’s Manchester derby, however, referee Stuart Attwell’s decision would not prove decisive. The game turned in Everton’s favour minutes later when Abdul Fatawu received a second yellow card for diving but, having failed to kill off Gary O’Neil’s 10 men, they ended up hanging on. VAR was therefore spared Moyes’s wrath. Continue reading...

About 30 detainees from the US remain trapped at a hotel in the outskirts of the coastal city of Malabo after being deported from the US. items.title: Kevin Warsh may be the adult in the room. But can he calm the US economy?

items.title: U.S. and Denmark reach deal to build U.S. military presence in Greenland
items.summary: President Trump says he has a deal with Denmark to bolster the U.S. military presence in Greenland. The announcement comes after months of threatening to take the island by force from the NATO ally.

items.title: Tech Now
items.summary: Adrienne Murray follows NASA scientists in Iceland researching a rare total solar eclipse.

items.title: Would Australians support a smart glasses ban?
items.summary: As Australia considers barring the use of smart glasses in government offices, the BBC asks people in Sydney what they think.
